quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the main travel area. Both vehicles need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see clearly again. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water instead of the road. To prevent this in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road's shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done leaving the bus.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is coming. Be careful when pedestrians may be in the area.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing downward is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop at a yield sign.

questions.question: This sign shows a railroad crossing with no signal. You should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At this type of railroad crossing, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be prepared to stop. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Longer than normal.
Shorter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep extra space between you and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your windows before driving. Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in work areas are the color:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Look for other vehicles in the space you want to enter. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and never try to drive around the crossing gates.

questions.question: What should you do to prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot lightly touching the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes focused on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on spotting problems early. Scan far ahead and also check the sides of the road. Do not just stare straight ahead at the center of the road.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop completely.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Position your vehicle parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the edge nearest you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Signal as you start to move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Vehicles and motorcycles often hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning on residential streets. Signal 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway ends.
A one-way street begins.
A one-way street ends.
A divided highway begins.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway begins.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead is divided by a median or divider. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. You can lose control of your vehicle. Slow down when you see this sign because it takes longer to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: How much of the road lane are motorcycles entitled to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars in these blind spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the roadway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the roadway, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it off the roadway completely if you can. All four wheels should be off the main-traveled part of the road.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. They override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A bicyclist is ahead going the same direction. How do you safely pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bike.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on high-speed roads. Do not honk, as it may scare the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, pulling into traffic from parking, pulling out of a parking space, and passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Driving too fast often:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Improves your ability to react to hazards.
Leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look into the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if no cars are coming
Where signs and road markings allow passing
On a curve if no cars are coming

questions.correctAnswerText: Where signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleys. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are near. Children may not understand danger and may run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other car in your mirror.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They give information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers information. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. More alcohol makes your judgment worse and your driving skills weaker. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have gates or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not necessary.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Why does night driving require more caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and drivers cannot see as well. From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Wait for time to pass.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly and leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise will not reduce your blood alcohol level. The only way to lower it is to wait.

questions.question: As you reach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop for the red light if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you see one deer or moose on the road, you will not see another.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Deer and moose often travel in groups. If one crosses the road, more are likely nearby and may cross after it.

questions.question: Driving has risk, so you should always work to improve your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: If drivers think they have nothing to learn, driving becomes unsafe. Always try to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: Not reporting an accident with property damage of $1,000 or more is not a crime.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If an accident causes property damage of $1,000 or more, you must report it to police or the sheriff. Any accident with injuries must also be reported. Failing to report an accident can result in criminal charges and license suspension.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.
Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give the full lane to the motorcycle. Do not share the lane. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: Stop at regular intervals on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you are not tired.

questions.question: What should you do at a broken traffic signal?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
You do not need to stop if the intersection is clear.
Drive quickly through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat it as an all-way stop. Always come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic violation.
Only if you are stopped for a traffic violation.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic violation.
questions.explanation: Always carry proof of insurance. You must show it to an officer after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: What should you do if a large vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Speed up.
Change lanes.
Keep your speed the same or slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same or slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when a large vehicle is passing you. Keep your speed the same or slow down slightly. This lets the larger vehicle pass safely.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to fix drowsiness.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before the turn is complete.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line on a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane without a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before driving forward.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even without a marked crosswalk.
